newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SGS sees lower 1997 net profit.
newsitem.headline: SGS sees lower 1997 net profit.

text.p: Swiss group Societe Generale de Surveillance Holding SA (SGS), the world leader in inspections and testing, said in a statement it expected to see 1997 group net profit decline from 1996 levels.
"Except for the termination of contracts with Indonesia, Pakistan and Nigeria, 1997 started well for the SGS group due to continued growth and positive foreign exchange impact," it said.
"Results for the first six months of 1997 should therefore be broadly in line with those of the same period last year.

"However, the full effect of the loss of earnings from the termination of those ...contracts will be felt during the second half of this year and thus the company foresees that the group's net profit in 1997 will be lower than that of 1996."
SGS said it stopped on April 1 all activity related to its preshipment import verification contract with Indonesia, which ended on March 31, as already announced.

It said shareholders renewed for one year a clause in company bylaws that authorises the board of directors to proceed with share buybacks at a price above market levels without a distribution of put options to all shareholders, as in 1993.
This stems from the fact that it remained unclear whether tax authorities would appeal the tax panel decision upholding SGS's position on such buybacks. The appeals deadline is June 9.
SGS posted a 1996 consolidated net profit of 262.7 million Swiss francs, up 14 percent from 1995.
